Docket 1.3.78

**A page that lists foreign titles is no longer called a foreign page.**

If you publish an index — a bookshelf, a catalogue, a directory — whose entries
happen to be in another language, Docket used to read the entries as the page
and tell you your English page was written in Dutch. It then offered to change
your `lang` attribute, which would have been the wrong fix to a problem you did
not have.

Measured on a public library site: 23 index pages received that advice. Every
one of them was an English page listing Dutch and French book titles.

The detection was never wrong — those titles really are Dutch. What was wrong
was whose words Docket thought they were. It now recognises when almost
everything it is reading sits inside links, which is what an index looks like
and what an article does not, and stays quiet.

A page genuinely written in a language it does not declare is still reported,
including one with a large navigation menu or a lot of links in its prose. The
threshold was set from measurements of real pages rather than picked: the index
pages sit above nine tenths link text, and encyclopedia articles — about the
most heavily linked writing there is — sit near a quarter in every language
tested.

This is the third time a check has mistaken quoted words for the page's own,
after restaurant addresses on a delivery site and tutor biographies on a
language-teaching marketplace. All three are now fixed.

99 checks across 13 areas.
